payload: {"ticket":"t-d052","title":"Battery plants that fail only under parallel load","items":3}

{"at":"2026-09-26T03:03:40Z","note":"Likely common cause (OW-WAR-0141's run: 00-corpus 'the page reaches for nothing' → exit 127, i.e. ./target/debug/war not found): plant-isolated.sh points every clone's target/ and CARGO_TARGET_DIR at the SAME build directory, and 89-schemas runs `cargo run` inside each clone. Each clone sits at a different path, so cargo sees changed sources and relinks target/debug/war while other batteries are executing it — a missing binary (127) or a half-written one (empty output, e.g. 54-intake's JSON). Parallel batteries sharing one target dir are unsound. Fix options: 89-schemas uses the built binary instead of cargo run; or plant-isolated gives each run its own target dir (a full build per run); or the gate refuses to run concurrently with itself (a lock). Receipts that PASSED in parallel are still sound (same commit, identical build); failures must be rerun serially."}

{"item":"i-c824","target":"t-d052/i-c824","on":"2026-09-26","note":"Confirmed mechanism, not the single instance: cargo uplifts target/debug/war by unlink() then linkat() (strace of a clone's cargo build), and an existence probe caught the path absent once during one relink; exec in that gap is exit 127 (0141's 00-corpus). war --json emits an envelope on every error path (checked), so 54-intake's empty stdout means the process never ran or was killed; its exit status is discarded (2>/dev/null, no $?), so the 0124 record cannot name which of the two plan runs failed, only that one did (one alias in the error). 89-schemas ran cargo run --features schema four times per battery from a clone at a new path, rebuilding and relinking each time; it also left a schema-featured war with a planted pack embedded (schemas/pack.json is include_str!'d) as target/debug/war for every later plant. Fix: battery_tool (lib.sh) builds schema-war and xtask into <target>/battery-tools under flock and runs private copies; target/debug/war's inode was unchanged across the solo run and all 3-wide rounds."}

{"item":"i-0fd7","target":"t-d052/i-0fd7","on":"2026-09-26","note":"67-pins-next: bound is next/status CPU (user+sys incl. git), interleaved, min of 3 each, < 3.4, plus a 15 s CPU backstop. Wall failed under load; plain CPU still moved 1.45x three-wide (hybrid i5-13600K: E-cores). Before t-280c ratio 4.3, after 2.35 (933448d2); at HEAD 2.48-2.64 solo and three-wide. Also found the corpus regressed (t-eca6): next 17 s CPU, status 68 s; fixed by a per-process tree-read memo for one-shot next/check/status."}
